subject: Physics
title: SI and dimensions
concept: A measurement is a number and a unit. Dimensions can reject a wrong equation. They cannot prove a right one.
q: Which check can dimensions do?
options: Reject an equation whose two sides have different dimensions
easy: Same dimensions are necessary. They are not sufficient.

subject: Physics
title: Error propagation
concept: Relative errors add when quantities multiply or divide. A power becomes a multiplier.
q: For \(Z=A^2/C^3\), the maximum relative error is
easy: Powers become multipliers. A negative power still adds in the maximum error.

subject: Physics
title: Resolution
concept: A vector in a plane is two perpendicular parts. The magnitude is the root of the sum of squares.
q: The magnitude of 3 i + 4 j is

subject: Physics
title: Average and instantaneous
concept: Average velocity is displacement over time. Instantaneous velocity is the slope of x against t.
q: If acceleration depends on velocity, you should
options: Separate variables. Do not use v=u+at
easy: Constant-acceleration formulas need constant a.

subject: Physics
title: Projectile
concept: Horizontal velocity is constant on level ground. Vertical motion has acceleration g downward.
q: Time to the top of a projectile is
easy: Vertical velocity falls from u sinθ to zero at rate g.

subject: Physics
title: Net force
concept: Acceleration is caused by the net force, not by one force. A constraint links accelerations.
q: Two blocks move together on a rough surface only if
options: Required friction is within the maximum static friction
easy: One acceleration needs enough friction, up to μN.

subject: Physics
title: Static and kinetic
concept: Static friction adjusts up to μs N. Kinetic friction is μk N and opposes sliding.
q: Static friction on a book at rest on a table is
options: Equal to the applied force, up to the maximum
easy: It matches the push until the limit.

subject: Physics
title: Variable force
concept: Work is force along displacement. For a variable force, add F dx.
q: Work by a variable force is
easy: Add the small pieces F dx.

subject: Physics
title: Potential curve
concept: For a conservative force, F = -dU/dx. A minimum of U is stable.
q: Stable equilibrium on a U-x curve is
easy: A minimum pushes the body back.

subject: Physics
title: Torque and rolling
concept: Torque is r cross F. Pure rolling on a fixed surface means the contact point is at rest, so v = Rω.
q: The no-slip condition on a fixed surface is
easy: Contact point at rest means v = Rω.

subject: Physics
title: Moment of inertia
concept: I measures how mass is spread from the axis. A cavity is treated as negative mass.
q: A hole cut from a disc moves the centre of mass
easy: Missing mass is negative mass.

subject: Physics
title: Inside a sphere
concept: Outside a sphere the field is like a point mass. Inside a uniform sphere the field is proportional to r.
q: Field inside a uniform solid sphere is
easy: Only the mass inside r pulls, and that mass grows as r cubed.

subject: Physics
title: Bernoulli and Torricelli
concept: Along a streamline, pressure, speed and height trade off. A small hole at depth h has efflux speed sqrt(2gh).
q: Efflux speed from a hole at depth h is
easy: The height drop becomes speed.

subject: Physics
title: Calorimetry
concept: Heat lost equals heat gained if the system is closed. A phase change uses latent heat at constant temperature.
q: Ice melting at 0°C absorbs heat
easy: Latent heat changes phase, not temperature.

subject: Physics
title: First law
concept: ΔU = Q + W with one sign convention. For an ideal gas, U depends only on temperature.
q: Free expansion of an ideal gas into vacuum has
easy: No heat and no external work, so U and T stay.

subject: Physics
title: rms speed
concept: Pressure comes from molecular collisions. rms speed is sqrt(3RT/M).
q: rms speed rises when
options: Molar mass rises at fixed T
easy: rms speed grows with the square root of T.

subject: Physics
title: SHM
concept: SHM means acceleration is minus a constant times displacement. A spring-mass period is 2π sqrt(m/k).
q: Two equal springs in series have effective k
easy: Series springs add extensions, so the combination is softer.

subject: Physics
title: Standing waves and beats
concept: A standing wave needs two equal waves in opposite directions. Beats are two close frequencies.
q: Beat frequency is
options: The difference of the two frequencies
easy: You hear the difference.

subject: Physics
title: Gauss
concept: Gauss's law is useful when symmetry makes E constant on a surface: sphere, long wire, infinite sheet.
q: Gauss is the fast tool for
options: A long wire or an infinite sheet
A dipole at a random point
easy: You need a surface where E is constant or zero.

subject: Physics
title: Series and parallel
concept: Series capacitors share charge. Parallel capacitors share voltage.
q: A battery stays connected as a dielectric is inserted. What rises?
easy: Voltage is fixed. Capacitance rises, so charge rises.

subject: Physics
title: Power transfer
concept: Current is charge per time. Maximum power to a load from a cell is when load resistance equals internal resistance.
q: Maximum power to the load when internal resistance is r occurs at
easy: P = I squared R, and I = E/(R+r). The peak is at R = r.

subject: Physics
title: Helix
concept: A charge with velocity perpendicular to B moves in a circle of radius mv/(qB). A parallel component makes a helix.
q: The cyclotron radius is
easy: Magnetic force supplies the centripetal force.

subject: Physics
title: Faraday and Lenz
concept: Induced emf equals minus the rate of change of flux. Lenz says the induced current opposes the change.
q: A rod sliding on rails in a uniform B has emf
easy: Area changes, so flux changes.

subject: Physics
title: Phase
concept: In a series LCR circuit, voltage and current are in phase at resonance. Impedance is then just R.
q: At resonance in series LCR
easy: The reactances cancel.

subject: Physics
title: E and B
concept: In a plane EM wave, E and B are perpendicular to each other and to the direction of travel. c = E/B.
q: E and B in a plane EM wave are
easy: They are perpendicular, and both are perpendicular to the ray.

subject: Physics
title: Thin lens
concept: 1/v - 1/u = 1/f. An object at the focus of a convex lens gives an image at infinity.
q: Object at the focus of a convex lens. The image is
easy: Rays from the focus leave parallel.

subject: Physics
title: Fringe width
concept: In Young's experiment, fringe width is λD/d. A sheet in one path shifts the pattern.
q: If slit separation d increases, fringe width
easy: β is inversely proportional to d.

subject: Physics
title: Photoelectric
concept: K_max = hν - φ. Below the threshold frequency, no electrons leave, however bright the light.
q: Stopping potential depends on
easy: Intensity changes the number of electrons, not the energy of each.

subject: Physics
title: Bohr
concept: The photon energy is the difference of two levels. Balmer lines end at n = 2.
q: A drop from n=3 to n=2 emits
options: E2 - E3 as a positive energy
easy: Emission energy is the higher level minus the lower.

subject: Physics
title: Binding and decay
concept: Binding energy per nucleon peaks near iron. N = N0 e^(-λt) means the same fraction is lost in every half-life.
q: After one half-life, N is
easy: Half-life is the time to halve, whatever N is.

subject: Physics
title: Forward bias
concept: A p-n junction conducts in forward bias, when the p side is at higher potential.
q: In forward bias, the p side is
easy: Forward bias lowers the barrier.

subject: Chemistry
title: Limiting reagent
concept: The mole counts particles. The limiting reagent is the one that runs out first.
q: Molarity changes with temperature because
easy: Moles stay. Volume expands, so molarity falls.

subject: Chemistry
title: Quantum numbers
concept: Four quantum numbers label an electron. n unpaired electrons give magnetic moment sqrt(n(n+2)).
q: A Balmer line ends at
easy: Balmer ends at 2. Lyman ends at 1.

subject: Chemistry
title: Trends
concept: Across a period, size generally falls and ionisation energy generally rises. There are known exceptions, such as N above O.
q: Ionisation energy of N is above O because
options: N has a half-filled p subshell
easy: The half-filled set is unusually stable.

subject: Chemistry
title: VSEPR
concept: Electron pairs stay as far apart as they can. A lone pair takes more room than a bond pair.
q: Water is bent because
easy: Four pairs, two of them lone, give a bent shape.

subject: Chemistry
title: Enthalpy
concept: ΔH is heat at constant pressure. Hess's law says the change depends on start and end, not the path.
q: Isothermal expansion of an ideal gas has
easy: U depends only on T for an ideal gas.

subject: Chemistry
title: Buffer
concept: K is fixed at a given temperature. A buffer resists pH change. pH = pKa + log(salt/acid) for a weak acid buffer.
q: A common ion on a weak acid
easy: The extra ion pushes the equilibrium back.

subject: Chemistry
title: Oxidation number
concept: Oxidation is a rise in oxidation number. Reduction is a fall. The two must balance in a redox equation.
q: In a redox equation
easy: Count the electrons on both sides.

subject: Chemistry
title: Carbocation
concept: Inductive, resonance and hyperconjugation decide stability. A more stable carbocation is easier to form.
q: Usually the most stable is
easy: Alkyl groups stabilise the positive carbon.

subject: Chemistry
title: Markovnikov
concept: Alkenes add HX by Markovnikov unless peroxide is present for HBr. Ozonolysis cuts the double bond.
q: Peroxide changes the addition of
easy: Only HBr has a useful peroxide path.

subject: Chemistry
title: Anomaly
concept: Lithium and beryllium differ from the rest of their groups because they are small and polarising.
q: Li differs from other alkali metals because
options: It is small and polarises anions
easy: Small size and high charge density.

subject: Chemistry
title: Colligative
concept: A colligative property depends on the number of particles, not their identity. The van't Hoff factor counts association or dissociation.
q: i is less than 1 when
options: The solution is ideal and i is forced to 1
easy: Association means fewer particles.

subject: Chemistry
title: Nernst
concept: Oxidation is on the left, reduction on the right. At 298 K, E = E° - (0.059/n) log Q.

subject: Chemistry
title: Order and half-life
concept: Order is experimental. A first-order half-life does not depend on concentration.
q: A first-order half-life is 10 min. After 20 min the reactant is
easy: Two half-lives leave one quarter.

subject: Chemistry
title: Colour and oxidation
concept: Transition-metal colour often comes from d-d transitions. Lanthanide contraction shrinks the later lanthanides.
q: A vacant or full d set usually means
easy: A d-d jump needs a partly filled d set.

subject: Chemistry
title: Crystal field
concept: Coordination number counts donor atoms. A strong-field ligand pairs electrons and gives low spin in an octahedral complex.
q: A strong-field octahedral ligand gives
easy: A large split makes pairing cheaper.

subject: Chemistry
title: SN1 and SN2
concept: SN2 inverts the carbon and is faster on a less hindered carbon. SN1 makes a carbocation and can racemise.
q: SN2 is fastest on
easy: The nucleophile needs room.

subject: Chemistry
title: Acidity
concept: Phenol is more acidic than ethanol because the phenoxide ion is resonance-stabilised.
q: Phenol is acidic because
options: The phenoxide ion spreads the charge
easy: The anion is stabilised by the ring.

subject: Chemistry
title: Aldol
concept: A nucleophile attacks the carbonyl carbon. An aldol needs an alpha hydrogen on the enolate partner.
q: A carbonyl with no alpha hydrogen cannot
options: Form an enolate for an aldol
easy: No alpha hydrogen means no enolate.

subject: Chemistry
title: Basicity
concept: In water, solvation and steric effects change the gas-phase basicity order. Aromatic amines are weaker bases.
q: Aniline is a weaker base than ethylamine because
options: The lone pair is delocalised into the ring
easy: The lone pair is shared with the ring.

subject: Chemistry
title: Reducing sugar
concept: A reducing sugar has a free hemiacetal. Sucrose does not, because both anomeric carbons are tied.
q: Sucrose is non-reducing because
easy: The anomeric carbons are locked.

subject: Chemistry
title: Packing
concept: Atoms in a crystal sit on a lattice. Octahedral and tetrahedral voids differ in number and size.
q: A void surrounded by six spheres is
easy: Six neighbours make an octahedral hole.

subject: Chemistry
title: Structures
concept: Know the shapes of the common oxoacids and xenon fluorides from the electron count, not from memory alone.
q: XeF2 is
easy: Five pairs, three of them lone, give a linear molecule.

subject: Mathematics
title: Venn
concept: Union is or. Intersection is and. A three-set problem needs the overlaps counted once.
q: n(A ∪ B) equals
easy: Add both, then remove the double-counted overlap.

subject: Mathematics
title: Domain
concept: The domain is the set of inputs that keep the expression defined. A square root needs a non-negative inside.
q: The domain of sqrt(x-2) is
easy: The inside of the root must be at least zero.

subject: Mathematics
title: General solution
concept: One angle is not the full solution. Add the period.
q: sin x = 1/2 needs
options: The principal angles plus the period
easy: The wave repeats.

subject: Mathematics
title: Modulus
concept: A complex number is a point. The modulus is the distance from the origin.

subject: Mathematics
title: Wavy curve
concept: On a number line, a rational inequality changes sign at each odd-multiplicity root.
q: A sign chart is used for
easy: Mark the critical points and test the sign.

subject: Mathematics
title: Order
concept: A permutation arranges. A combination selects. Order matters only in the first.
q: Ways to choose 2 from 5

subject: Mathematics
title: General term
concept: The general term of (a+b)^n is C(n,r) a^(n-r) b^r. The r starts at 0.
q: The term with b^r has coefficient
easy: Pick r factors of b and the rest a.

subject: Mathematics
title: AM-GM
concept: An AP has a constant difference. A GP has a constant ratio. For positive numbers, AM is at least GM.
q: AM - GM for positive numbers is
easy: Equality when the numbers are equal.

subject: Mathematics
title: Slope
concept: Slope is rise over run. Parallel lines have equal slopes. Perpendicular lines have slopes whose product is -1.
q: Parallel lines have
easy: Same slope means same direction.

subject: Mathematics
title: Parabola
concept: A parabola is equidistant from a focus and a directrix. For y^2=4ax the focus is (a,0).
q: Focus of y^2=4ax is
easy: The focus is a units from the vertex.

subject: Mathematics
title: Standard limit
concept: A limit is the value approached. Plug-in is not allowed when it gives 0/0.
q: lim x→0 sin x / x is
easy: This standard limit is 1.

subject: Mathematics
title: Events
concept: Mutually exclusive events cannot happen together. Independent events do not change each other's chance.
q: For mutually exclusive A and B, P(A and B) is
easy: They cannot happen together.

subject: Mathematics
title: Equivalence
concept: Reflexive, symmetric and transitive together make an equivalence relation.
q: An equivalence relation must be
easy: All three.

subject: Mathematics
title: Principal value
concept: Each inverse trig function has one principal branch. Stay inside that branch.
q: The principal value of arcsin is in
easy: arcsin returns an angle in that closed interval.

subject: Mathematics
title: Multiplication
concept: Matrix multiplication is row by column. It is not commutative.
q: AB = BA is
options: True only if A is zero
easy: Order matters.

subject: Mathematics
title: Singular
concept: A zero determinant means the rows are dependent and there is no inverse.
q: If det A = 0, AX=B
easy: No inverse means not one unique solution.

subject: Mathematics
title: Corner
concept: Continuity means the limit equals the value. A corner can be continuous and still not differentiable.
q: |x| at 0 is
easy: The graph is joined. The slope jumps.

subject: Mathematics
title: Increasing
concept: f' > 0 on an interval means f is increasing there.
q: If f'(x) > 0 on an interval, f is
easy: Positive slope means the value rises.

subject: Mathematics
title: Antiderivative
concept: An indefinite integral is a family of antiderivatives. Differentiating it returns the integrand.
q: The derivative of ∫ f is
easy: They undo each other.

subject: Mathematics
title: Between curves
concept: The area between two curves is the integral of the upper minus the lower, between the intersection points.
q: Area between curves uses
easy: Subtract the lower from the upper.

subject: Mathematics
title: Integrating factor
concept: dy/dx + P y = Q is solved by multiplying by e to the integral of P.
q: The integrating factor is
easy: It makes the left side a product rule.

subject: Mathematics
title: Dot and cross
concept: The dot product is a scalar. The cross product is a vector perpendicular to both.
q: a · b = 0 means
options: They are perpendicular, if neither is zero
easy: Zero dot product means a right angle.

subject: Mathematics
title: Skew lines
concept: A line needs a point and a direction. Skew lines do not meet and are not parallel.
q: Skew lines
options: Do not meet and are not parallel
easy: If they were coplanar and did not meet, they would be parallel.

subject: Mathematics
title: Bayes
concept: Conditional probability is the chance given that something already happened. Bayes updates a prior.
q: P(A|B) is
easy: Condition on B, so divide by P(B).

subject: Mathematics
title: Corner
concept: A linear objective on a polygonal region reaches its max or min at a corner.
q: Check the objective at
easy: The extreme is at a vertex.
